I am a 57-year-old woman farming in Oromia. This barley plot is small, only 0.17 hectares, but barley is our staple food and I know it grows better with some fertilizer. I will buy a small amount of DAP and urea from the cooperative — not the full package, because money is tight, but enough to help the crop. I have manure from our animals too, so I will spread that on the field before planting. I have my own barley seed saved from last year; it grows well here and I do not trust the new varieties. I have my children to help me, so we can manage the work ourselves without hiring anyone. We do not have irrigation here — we depend on the rains — and I have never used chemicals for pests on barley.
